title: Honest AI-unavailable handling end to end: backend 503 AI_UNAVAILABLE, accurate provider status, desktop notice on every AI surface
goal: When no AI provider is available, the product must say so plainly everywhere instead of returning stub text as if it were an AI answer.
context: Added by the orchestrator 2026-10-06 from desktop/audit/fix/requests/B28.md. Today backend/src/services/ai-router.ts (around lines 190, 216, 249) returns HTTP 200 with a stub payload `{"note":"Cloudflare AI not available in this environment. Configure Workers AI binding."}` when the Workers AI binding is missing or non-functional; `/ai/extract-lead`, `/ai/generate-itinerary`, `/ai/compose-message` pass that through, and `/ai/intelligence/nl-query` turns it into a misleading 'I couldn't generate a query' narrative. `GET /ai/settings` reports provider.cloudflare = true unconditionally. B28 (merged) worked around it on the desktop: `desktop/src/lib/api/ai.ts` detects the stub and throws `AiUnavailableError`; `components/domain/ai/AiUnavailableNotice` renders a friendly 'AI is not configured yet' state with Try again on the lead-creation, itinerary and compose pages. NL Search and the BI pages have no such handling. Baselines: backend vitest 41 files / 1087 passed, tsc 0; desktop tsc 0, unit 1232, lint ratchet (desktop/audit/fix/lint-baseline.json). The local/test backend has NO AI binding (the e2e wrangler config strips [ai]), so 'unavailable' is the state every local run and the demo recording will see unless a provider key is configured.
steps: Backend: in ai-router.ts replace the stub returns with a typed error (e.g. class AiUnavailableError extends Error with code 'AI_UNAVAILABLE'). Every AI route that calls the router (grep callers under backend/src/routes: ai*.ts, chatbot, communications compose, extractions, intelligence incl. nl-query, business intelligence/briefings) must translate it into HTTP 503 with the standard envelope {success:false,error:{code:'AI_UNAVAILABLE',message:'AI is not configured for this workspace yet.'}}. Never return stub text as content. Usage/quota counters must not be incremented for an unavailable call.

Before changing statuses: grep packages/shared/lib and packages/crm_app/lib (Flutter CRM app) for these endpoints. If the Flutter app reads the stub/200, keep it working - a 503 with error.message is acceptable only if the app already shows error.message for non-2xx (verify in its ApiClient error handling); otherwise report precisely instead of breaking it.

Backend GET /ai/settings: provider.cloudflare (and any other provider flag) must reflect reality - true only when the binding/key exists (and, if cheaply detectable, is functional). Additive field `available: boolean` summarising whether any provider can serve requests.

Backend tests: with no AI binding (the vitest env) each affected endpoint returns 503 AI_UNAVAILABLE (update existing tests that asserted the 200 stub - list them); /ai/settings reports cloudflare false / available false; quota unchanged after a 503.

Desktop lib/api/ai.ts (and any other client that calls AI endpoints: chatbot.ts, communications.ts compose, extractions, intelligence): map HTTP 503 with code AI_UNAVAILABLE to the existing AiUnavailableError; keep the stub detection as a fallback for older backends. Unit-test it.

Desktop pages: show AiUnavailableNotice (existing component) on every AI surface that can hit the provider - NL Search, AI Business Intelligence / briefings, AI Intelligence widgets, AI Extractions actions, chatbot test/preview if any, compose-with-AI in SendMessageDialog - instead of an error toast or a fake answer. Use `available` from /ai/settings to show the notice up-front where sensible (no request needed).
Run gates; look at NL Search and one BI page in screenshots (light + dark).
acceptance: No backend AI endpoint returns stub text; without a provider they return 503 AI_UNAVAILABLE and do not consume quota.
Every desktop AI surface shows the friendly notice (no error toast, no fake answer) when AI is unavailable.
backend vitest 0 failed, passed >= 1087; backend tsc 0; desktop typecheck 0, unit pass, lint ratchet pass with 0 errors in files you touch; build pass; ai-*.spec.ts pass.
notes: Demo implication (report it): unless a real AI key is configured for the recording, AI chapters in the walkthrough will show the 'not configured' state - say exactly which env vars / bindings make AI live locally (backend/.dev.vars key names only, never values).
